rv.q: Dorian , written by Phoebe Eclair-Powell and Owen Horsley, is a complete triumph in every way.
It’s a brilliant and electrically charged drama, laced with dark comedy, that’s both scholarly and cerebral, intelligent and erotic.
Holland creates a show that is both enchanting and full of bitter heartbreak, highlighted by Wilde's lonely downfall.
DORIAN fuses gothic horror, biting satire, and cabaret flair into an unforgettable night of theatre.
Stylish, gritty, funny, and bold, Dorian reminds us, as Wilde did, that 'the truth is rarely pure, and never simple.'
Dorian , by Open Space Arts, is more than a clever retelling of a literary classic; it is a defiant act of queer remembrance.

cn.t: Critics praise this inventive, queer adaptation as bold and electrically charged, blending Wilde's novel with his biography through wit and contemporary style. The intimate production earns acclaim for its creative energy and cerebral storytelling.
